title: Applied ML Evals: Comprehensive Onboarding and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Raman
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes Redwood's integrated process for onboarding models into the eval-harness, creating and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, establishing quality guardrails, selecting and validating quantization profiles, and running regression triage when degradations occur. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML, and platform engineers who own model onboarding and quality monitoring.

Scope:
- Covers models intended for Redwood Hosted and Dedicated serving.
- Applies to open and customer-provided models (FP32, INT8/4 quantized variants, and model-splits).
- Excludes experimental research models unless explicitly promoted for serving.

Goals:
1. Ensure repeatable onboarding with automated evals and clear acceptance criteria.
2. Detect and triage regressions quickly with reproducible tests and rollback guidance.
3. Maintain a catalog of prompt sets, benchmarks, and quantization profiles tied to SLOs and cost targets.

Ownership and roles:
- Playbook owner: Applied ML (playbook steward: Priya Raman).
- Model owner: team that requests onboarding (must provide model artifact, weights, and license metadata).
- Eval harness owner: Eng - Eval Infrastructure (Pager: eng-eval infra oncall).
- Regression triage lead: Applied ML rotation.

High-level workflow (steps):
1) Intake and eligibility check
   - Submit model intake form (internal link: /tools/model-intake) with model name, version, architecture, and target use-cases.
   - Required fields: model artifact S3/GCS path, license, training data notes, recommended temperature/decoding settings, expected latency profile.
   - Acceptance gate: model must pass quick security scan (no known unsafe license) and smoke load test (90th pct latency < target hardware-specific threshold).

2) Eval-harness onboarding
   - Create an eval job in the eval-harness repo using the standard template: eval_job.yaml. Minimal fields: model_id, model_variant, prompt_set_ids, metrics_to_compute.
   - Baseline metrics: perplexity (if applicable), BLEU/ROUGE where relevant, task-specific accuracy, toxicity and safety coverage, factuality proxies (QA exact match / F1).
   - Example eval command:
     ./eval_harness/run_eval.sh --model s3://redwood-models/gnn-20b/2026-09-01 --prompts prompt-set://customer-support-v1 --out results/gnn-20b-cs-2026-09-01.json

3) Prompt set and benchmarks guidance
   - Prompt sets must include:
     - Canonical prompts (20-200 examples) representing core user flows.
     - Edge-case prompts (10-50) capturing adversarial/long-tail requests.
     - Regression sentinel prompts (5-20) for quick smoke tests.
   - Benchmarks must be versioned and stored in prompt-catalog (catalog entry format specified in the prompt-sets template).
   - Naming convention: <domain>-<usecase>-vYYYYMMDD. Example: customer-support-summary-v20261001.

4) Quality guardrails and acceptance criteria
   - Required guardrails for production promotion:
     - Task accuracy >= baseline_model_accuracy - 2% (absolute) OR meets team-negotiated SLA.
     - Toxicity/unsafe output rate < 0.5% (measured on safety suite).
     - Semantic drift: top-1 intent accuracy degradation < 3% vs baseline.
     - Latency SLO: p95 < hardware_target_ms (see Hardware SLO table below).
   - Acceptance checklist (must be green): automated evals, manual review for 50 sampled outputs across canonical prompts, cost estimate within budget (see cost guidance).

5) Quantization profiles and validation
   - Profile catalog entry fields: model_id, quant_profile_id, expected memory reduction, quality delta (vs FP32), supported hardware, recommended batch sizes.
   - Standard profiles: fp32, fp16, int8-quant, int4-quant (when supported).
   - Validation steps:
     1. Unit tests: forward pass smoke for 100 random seeds.
     2. Eval harness: run prompt-set canonical and sentinel prompts; compute delta metrics (accuracy, logits-similarity).
     3. Regression belt: flag if quality delta > configured thresholds (default: accuracy drop > 2% or semantic-similarity < 0.95).
   - Example quant test command:
     ./quant_test/run_quant_validation.sh --model s3://redwood-models/gnn-20b --profile int8-01 --prompts prompt-set://customer-support-v1 --out quant-results/gnn-20b-int8-2026-10-20.json

6) Regression triage playbook (when a regression alert fires)
   - Triggering signals (examples):
     - CI eval failing against canonical prompt sets.
     - Monitoring alert: sudden drop in production quality score (defined metric drop > 2 stddev or > 3% absolute).
     - Customer report flagged as regression with attached example.
   - Immediate actions (first 30 minutes):
     1. Incident lead confirms scope and assigns triage channel (#prod-regression).
     2. Roll forward: if recent rollout present, initiate automatic rollback to last-known-good model variant and record action.
     3. Capture failing inputs from production (up to 200 examples) and run them through eval-harness to reproduce.
   - Reproduction (0-4 hours):
     - Run eval-harness with the production traffic sample, with identical tokenization, temperature, and decoding settings.
     - Compare outputs between current model and last-known-good using the regression diff tool (diff-tool v1.3).
   - Root cause categories to consider:
     - Model quality regression (training or model drift).
     - Quantization degradation (profile mismatch or precision loss).
     - Prompt set coverage gap (new user behavior not covered).
     - Serving/config change (tokenization, pre/post-processing, decoding params).
     - Data/regression introduced by model conversion pipeline.
   - Remediation steps by category:
     - Quality: revert to previous model, open model investigation ticket, schedule re-train if necessary.
     - Quantization: revert to higher-precision profile, re-run quantization with updated config, add sentinel tests to pipeline.
     - Prompt coverage: add failing examples to prompt-set and create targeted unit tests.
     - Serving/config change: revert change, add regression unit tests to CI.
   - Postmortem: required for regressions that cause customer impact or > 6 hours degradation. Postmortem must include timeline, RCA, corrective actions, and preventive tasks.

SLOs, thresholds and hardware targets (excerpt):
| Hardware class | Target p95 latency (ms) | Target p50 latency (ms) | Notes |
|----------------|-------------------------|-------------------------|-------|
| GPU-small (A10)| 120                     | 40                      | baseline for small models |
| GPU-medium (A100)| 60                   | 15                      | medium models and most production traffic |
| GPU-large (H100)| 30                    | 8                       | high-throughput low-latency tier |

Quality thresholds (examples):
- Safety: unsafe rate < 0.5% measured on safety-suite-v2.
- Factuality: closed-book QA exact match >= 70% on factuality-benchmark-v1 for knowledge-heavy models.
- Consistency: logits-cosine-similarity >= 0.95 between unquantized and quantized for sentinel prompts.

CI and automation checklist:
- Add eval job to eval-harness with nightly runs (registered in eval-job-registry).
- Include sentinel prompt regression tests in pre-merge CI pipeline.
- Add canary traffic route for first 24-72 hours of production exposure.
- Dashboard: create per-model panel in eval-dashboard with these widgets: quality-trend (7d), latency-percentiles, cost-per-token estimate, regression-alerts.

Template artifacts (examples to copy from templates folder):
- eval_job.yaml (fields: model_id, model_variant, prompt_set_ids, metrics, schedule)
- prompt_set_template.json (fields: id, name, domain, example_prompts[], tags[])
- quant_profile_template.yaml (fields: profile_id, params, supported_kernels)

Rollout checklist (pre-production):
1. All automated evals passing for canonical & sentinel prompt sets.
2. Manual review of 50 outputs across canonical prompts (signed off by model owner + applied ML reviewer).
3. Quantization profile validated and logged in profile-catalog.
4. Latency and cost estimates validated against target hardware.
5. Monitoring dashboards created and regression alerts configured.

Appendices:
A. Quick reproduction commands
- Download sample traffic and run eval-harness:
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-samples/traffic/last-24h.json ./samples/traffic-24h.json
  ./eval_harness/run_eval.sh --model-id gnn-20b --input ./samples/traffic-24h.json --out ./results/repro-gnn-20b.json

B. Useful internal tools and services
- eval-harness (repo: git@internal:redwood/eval-harness.git)
- prompt-catalog service (docs: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks)
- quantization service: quant-svc (internal API: POST /quantize/validate)
- regression diff tool: diff-tool v1.3 (repo: git@internal:redwood/diff-tool.git)

C. Related policies and links
- Model intake form: /tools/model-intake
- Security scan: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging
- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025

D. Example prompt-set entry (text representation)
Name: customer-support-summary-v20261001
Tags: customer-support, summarization, canonical
Canonical prompts: 100 examples covering email-summary, chat-summary, and case-notes-summary.
Sentinel prompts: 10 adversarial or edge-case examples (long thread, mixed languages, code snippets).

Notes and next steps:
- We will iterate on default thresholds for quantization-delta and quality drop during Q4 2026 based on observed false-positive rate in regression alerts.
- Proposed automation: add an automatic candidate-rollback policy for quantized profiles that fail sentinel similarity checks during early canary exposure.

If you have questions or need an onboarding slot, contact the Applied ML rotation (applied-ml-rotation@redwood.ai) or open a ticket in the Model Onboarding backlog (project: MBO).
